title: Robust Amortized Simulation-Based Inference via Learned Error Models
claim: A staged workflow pretrains on simulated data, then jointly learns a correction from real observations, then fine-tunes the posterior on corrected pairs.
layout: 2 rows, left-to-right with wrap-around arrow, three numbered stage banners
description: Two rows of rounded boxes connected by blue arrows, with a bent arrow carrying the flow from the end of row one to the start of row two. Row one has the prior, simulator, simulated pairs table, a frozen pretrained likelihood network and the NPE initialization posterior. Each box has a bold title with notation above it, such as p(θ), p(x|θ) and q_φ0(θ|x). A banner below labels the row '1 PRETRAIN (simulator pairs only)'. Row two starts with colored observation time series, then the joint IWAE fit block with q_φ and p_α feeding L_IWAE. Next come the frozen learned-correction ellipse, the corrected pairs table, NPE fine-tuning and the final posterior surface. Banners '2 JOINT IWAE FIT' and '3 FINE-TUNE' sit underneath. Snowflake icons mark frozen components. Teal, blue and navy colors tie the data together. The eye goes first to the top-left prior surface and follows the arrows.
caption: RVNP training and inference workflow. A simulator likelihood and posterior are pretrained on simulated pairs. The error model and posterior are then fitted jointly using unlabeled observations, followed by posterior fine-tuning with the learned correction fixed.
abstract: Recent advances in neural density estimation have enabled amortized Bayesian inference for complex stochastic simulators. However, these methods rely on simulators accurately reflecting the true data-generating process and can degrade significantly under model misspecification. We consider the setting where multiple unlabeled observations are available and introduce robust variational neural posterior estimation (RVNP), an amortized Bayesian inference method that uses an importance-weighted autoencoder to jointly learn a misspecification-robust posterior proxy and an explicit error model that captures the simulation-to-reality gap. Our results show that RVNP can recover robust posterior inference in a data-driven and interpretable manner, outperforming previous methods on multiple metrics across misspecified benchmarks.
